_notes.units: USD per 1M tokens. Keyed by chat_models KEY (e.g. opus5.5), not the Bedrock model id.
_notes.cache_write: prompt-cache write, at the rate of the TTL the app actually sends. Anthropic: the app sends a 1-hour TTL to every Claude model (server/chat/caching.py), and Bedrock bills a 1-hour write at 2x input (a 5-minute write is 1.25x), so the rows carry the 1-hour rate. OpenAI: mantle reports cache_write_tokens inside input_tokens, and GPT-6 bills those 30-minute writes at 1.25x input (Cost Explorer bills almost all of their uncached prompt this way, with or without a cache key).
_notes.cached_in_input: true for OpenAI-on-Bedrock: input_tokens already INCLUDES the cached and the cache-written input, so each portion is billed once (at cache_read and cache_write), never also at the input rate.
_notes.gpt_billing: GPT rows are list rates. AWS billed GPT on Bedrock at $0 for this account as of 2026-09-23 (Cost Explorer: metered, UnblendedCost 0, no credit records), so every GPT figure the app shows is an estimate at list rates and is labelled that way.
_notes.gpt6.1-sol: Bedrock model card, Regional (bedrock-mantle serves it In-Region in us-east-1 only), prompts up to 272K: input $2.20 / output $11 / cached $0.11 / cache write $2.75 (2026-10-03).
_notes.gpt6-astra: Bedrock model card, In-Region (bedrock-mantle serves Astra In-Region in us-east-1 and us-west-2), prompts up to 272K: input $11 / output $55 / cached $1.10 / 30-minute cache write $13.75.
_notes.gpt6-luna: Derived, not yet published by AWS: OpenAI's list rates for prompts up to 272K tokens ($0.10 / $0.50 / cached $0.01 / cache write $0.125) plus the 10% fee every Bedrock OpenAI model card states for Commercial In-Region, which is what bedrock-mantle calls are. The AWS Price List, Bedrock pricing page and model cards carried no GPT-6 Luna row at its 2026-09-22 launch; switch to the card rates once published and re-check against the first invoice. Its long-context tier follows the same derivation: 2x input and cache, 1.5x output.
_notes.long_context: Every Bedrock OpenAI card bills a call whose prompt is over 272K input tokens at its long-context rates, on ALL of that call's tokens: 2x input, cache read and cache write, 1.5x output (GPT-6 Astra $22 / $82.50 / $2.20 / $27.50; GPT-6.1 Sol $4.40 / $16.50 / $0.22 / $5.50; GPT-6 Luna $0.22 / $0.825 / $0.022 / $0.275). The context_window only sets when compaction starts, so single rounds do go over it; long_context.above is that break and each row is priced at its own tier.
_notes.opus5.5: Bedrock global rates from the AWS Price List (Claude Opus 5.5, us-east-1, 2026-09-23), matching Anthropic's list price: $4 / $20 / cache read $0.20 / 1-hour cache write $8 (the TTL the app sends; the 5-minute write is $5).
_notes.sonnet5.5: AWS Price List (AmazonBedrockFoundationModels, us-east-1, Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Amazon Bedrock Edition), global usagetypes, 2026-09-29): $2 / $10 / cache read $0.20 / 1-hour cache write $4 (the TTL the app sends; the 5-minute write is $2.50).
_notes.fable5.1: AWS Price List (global): $10 / $50 / cache read $0.25 / 1-hour write $20.
_notes.nova-sonic: AWS Price List (AmazonBedrock, us-east-1, Nova Sonic 2.0), matching Cost Explorer's unit costs: speech input $0.003 / speech output $0.012 / text input $0.00033 / text output $0.00275 per 1K tokens. Speech and text bill apart, so the voice log records them under <model id>:speech and <model id>:text.
_notes.cohere: AWS Price List (AmazonBedrockFoundationModels, us-east-1): Cohere Embed 4 input $0.12 per 1M tokens, no output. The index calls it through its global profile (global.cohere.embed-v4:0) since 2026-09-28; the Price List carries no separate global Cohere rate, so that row repeats the in-region one, and the in-region row stays so earlier cost rows keep their price. Cohere Rerank 3.5 bills $0.002 per search unit, not per token, so its token rows carry no rate and show as $0 with the unpriced note.
_notes.override: To override or add rates, create pricing.json (gitignored, in the config folder: ~/.whisper for the Mac app, the repo root for a source install) holding only the keys you change. Entries there REPLACE these per model key; models you don't list keep the defaults below. An entry equal to a rate an earlier release shipped for that key is ignored (older installs seeded a full copy of this file), so a stale copy never shadows a correction. There is no silent fallback: a model with no entry bills $0 and logs loudly. Changes apply on server restart.
